title: Intelligence Brief
subtitle: The EU AI Act's Article 50 transparency/labeling d, The same week the EU's AI-content-disclosure law g, Minnesota's first-of-its-kind ban on AI 'nudify' a

insights.text: The EU AI Act's Article 50 transparency/labeling duties and the Commission's power to fine GPAI providers (up to EUR15M or 3% of global turnover) both activate today, August 2, 2026 -- while the broader high-risk AI system rules were separately deferred to December 2027 (Annex III) and August 2028 (Annex I) via the Digital Omnibus amendment adopted this June.

The same week the EU's AI-content-disclosure law gains enforcement teeth, three unrelated incidents show why it exists: YouTuber Hank Green (3.2M subscribers) apologized after viewers caught an unedited ChatGPT response embedded in his video script; Snapchat stopped recommending fully AI-generated Spotlight videos to non-followers; and Google paused its new Earth AI feature one day after launch once users generated fake satellite imagery, including a fabricated collapsed Eiffel Tower.

Minnesota's first-of-its-kind ban on AI 'nudify' apps took effect August 1 after a federal judge denied xAI's request to block it -- ruling turned on timing (xAI sued nearly three months after the law was signed, three days before it took effect) rather than the law's merits; a preliminary-injunction hearing on the substantive challenge is set for August 19.

Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters, ~1.56TB of memory at 4-bit) gets its first dollar-denominated hardware number: AMD's MI355X runs at $2.50/GPU-hr against Nvidia's B300 at $6.00/GPU-hr -- a 2.4x cost advantage for AMD despite B300 delivering roughly 1.65x more aggregate throughput. Separately, an unverified Reddit post claims K3 was run on a single 8GB-RAM CPU.

zhaoxuya520/reverse-skill, a reverse-engineering/pentesting 'skill router' for Claude Code, Kiro, Cursor, and Cline, hit GitHub Trending #4 today at +1,320 stars/day -- the highest velocity of any repo on the board, ahead of the #1 overall entry -- extending the packaged-skill genre into a security-research vertical for the first time. Created just 2.5 months ago (2026-05-13), now at 12,079 total stars.

Today's single highest-voted Hacker News story (467 points/160 comments, ahead of every other story on the board) is a resurfacing 2023 essay arguing Google followed an 'Embrace, Extend, Extinguish' pattern against RSS -- acquiring FeedBurner then gutting it, silently removing Chrome's RSS button, and killing Google Reader in 2013 -- paired same-day with 'Atom is better than RSS, in ways that matter,' anchoring Sunday's Content Aggregation rotation.

TencentCloud/TencentDB-Agent-Memory debuts on GitHub Trending (#13, +227/day, 10,387 total) as 'a team-level memory hub for AI Agents,' extending the crowded agent-memory-as-infrastructure race this stream has tracked since April with a new large-vendor entrant.

Hugging Face's own huggingface/speech-to-speech local-voice-agent toolkit decelerates on GitHub Trending to +442 stars/day (10,269 total), down from its 07-31 debut velocity of +628/day -- still growing, first deceleration logged for this entry.

takeaway.text: A regulator's enforcement power activates the same week three unrelated actors -- a creator, a platform, a frontier lab's own product team -- get caught by the disclosure problem it targets, a state nudify-app ban survives its first court test, an open-weight model gets its first real dollar-cost number against frontier silicon, a packaged-skill genre extends into security research, and Sunday's rotation is anchored by a three-year-old essay about the platform that helped kill the open web's original aggregation protocol.
